consumer: A dialogue/mission/eligibility possession check asking 'does the avatar have a 1st_aid?' — the engine's own has_amount/has_item_with/charges_of computation, not a raw item enumeration.
scope: A full possession reach that recurses into worn/wielded container contents and aggregates charges, matching the engine's has_amount/charges_of, not just top-level wielded/worn/inventory stacks.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — iterates only ctx.u.wielded_items(), ctx.u.worn, and ctx.u.inv_const_slice() top-level stacks, dumping raw item fields (S-class), so the frontend must re-derive the predicate from a partial view.
divergence: A 1st_aid stored inside a worn backpack (container nested in worn): the engine possession check reports HAS, but write_carried_items only emits the top-level container and never the nested kit, so the frontend re-derives 'not holding' — a false negative.
